bugs.name: Annual Revenue numeric filter activates nonnumeric text without validation
bugs.summary: The basic Annual Revenue filter accepts abc as an active numeric condition and empties the table without identifying the invalid value.
bugs.expected: The numeric filter prevents a nonnumeric draft from becoming an active numeric condition, instead of presenting an empty result as though the condition were valid.
bugs.actual: Entering abc leaves an active Annual Revenue ≥ abc chip and No Company found with no validation explanation. The rendered input is text despite the caller requesting number, and letter-valued conditions reach the query as a null numeric operand. Valid numeric thresholds filter the same control records correctly.
reproSteps: Create disposable Companies with distinct known Annual Revenue amounts, including zero, and isolate them using a search filter.
Add a basic Annual Revenue Greater than or equal condition and verify a valid numeric threshold selects the expected records.
Replace the numeric value with abc, dismiss the popup and inspect the active chip, table and validation feedback.
Repeat the invalid draft and compare another valid threshold and retained zero-USD control.

bugs.name: Calendar Date field checks Creation date while cards still use Due Date
bugs.summary: Returning a Due Date Tasks Calendar through Kanban leaves the selected Date field and card placement using different fields.
bugs.expected: The calendar Date field checkmark and the field used to place its cards stay consistent after layout changes.
bugs.actual: After Calendar→Kanban→Calendar, the saved view and Date field menu select Creation date, but the existing cards remain on their Due Date days. A fresh Table-only round trip keeps the menu and placement consistent; reload makes the affected calendar follow the saved field.
reproSteps: Create own Tasks whose Due Dates differ clearly from their Creation dates. Create a fresh Tasks Calendar using Due Date and verify matching placement/checkmark.
Switch through a Kanban layout grouped by Status, then return to Calendar without reloading.
Open Options → Date field and compare the checked Creation date with cards still placed on Due Dates. Repeat on another fresh view.
Compare a fresh Calendar→Table→Calendar round trip and a full reload of the affected view.

bugs.name: Deleting a saved view skips its documented confirmation
bugs.summary: The saved-view Delete actions immediately remove the view instead of offering the documented confirmation step.
bugs.expected: Selecting Delete for a saved view asks for confirmation before removing that configuration.
bugs.actual: A single click on Delete view in Options, or Delete in the view-picker ellipsis menu, immediately switches to All People and removes the saved custom People Table view. It remains absent after reload, with no confirmation dialog offered.
reproSteps: Create a disposable custom People Table view and reload to verify it is saved.
Open Options and click Delete view once. Observe the immediate switch and absence of a confirmation step.
Reload and check the picker: the deleted view is absent. Repeat on a separate saved view through its picker ellipsis → Delete.
Compare a saved control view: open Options, dismiss it without deleting, and reload; it remains available.

bugs.name: Company Name Is empty gives a wrong searched header count
bugs.summary: With an Any field search matching three fresh Companies, adding Name Is empty correctly renders zero rows but leaves a nonzero header count. Matching Name Is not empty and other filter controls work.
bugs.expected: The header count should apply the same basic Name filter and search combination as the displayed Company rows.
bugs.actual: With an Any field search matching three fresh Companies, adding Name Is empty correctly renders zero rows but leaves a nonzero header count. Matching Name Is not empty and other filter controls work.
reproSteps: Create fresh Companies with distinct nonempty names sharing a search token.
Apply Any field search for the token and add basic Name Is empty.
Compare the empty Table with its nonzero header count; test complementary and ordinary-filter controls.

bugs.name: Grouped Company select-all overstates the selected count
bugs.summary: In an Account Owner-grouped Company Table with only configured owner groups, select-all reports hundreds more selected than the displayed groups and Count all totals. Ordinary filtered and ungrouped controls report the correct selected count.
bugs.expected: The selected-count indicator should agree with the actual selectable records in the configured grouped view.
bugs.actual: In an Account Owner-grouped Company Table with only configured owner groups, select-all reports hundreds more selected than the displayed groups and Count all totals. Ordinary filtered and ungrouped controls report the correct selected count.
reproSteps: Open a Company Table grouped by Account Owner and configure only selected owner groups.
Compare visible group totals and Count all, then click the header selection checkbox.
Observe the selected-count overstatement. Compare an ordinary filtered view and an ungrouped Table.

bugs.name: Wide pinned Name covers later columns after narrowing the Table
bugs.summary: After widening Company Name to about 400px on desktop and scrolling right, narrowing to 390px leaves Name covering the viewport and later-column values and footer. Scrolling fully left and back compacts Name and exposes the values.
bugs.expected: The pinned Name column should compact on narrow layouts so horizontal scrolling can expose the later columns.
bugs.actual: After widening Company Name to about 400px on desktop and scrolling right, narrowing to 390px leaves Name covering the viewport and later-column values and footer. Scrolling fully left and back compacts Name and exposes the values.
reproSteps: On a desktop Company Table, widen Name to about 400px and scroll horizontally right.
Narrow the viewport to 390px while preserving horizontal scroll.
Observe later-column values and aggregates remain covered. Scroll fully left and back right as a recovery control.

bugs.name: New matching Person is absent from the searched Table until reload
bugs.summary: Creating and naming a Person to match an Any field search increases the header count but leaves the new row absent after closing its panel. Reload reveals the saved record; basic Name-filter and unfiltered controls insert it immediately.
bugs.expected: A saved newly created matching Person should appear in the active searched Table without requiring reload.
bugs.actual: Creating and naming a Person to match an Any field search increases the header count but leaves the new row absent after closing its panel. Reload reveals the saved record; basic Name-filter and unfiltered controls insert it immediately.
reproSteps: Apply an Any field search in a People Table.
Create a fresh Person and give it a matching name through the record panel.
Close the panel and compare increased count with missing row; reload to reveal it. Repeat with fresh data and compare basic Name-filter and unfiltered controls.

bugs.name: Second Ctrl+A leaves offscreen Table rows selected
bugs.summary: Pressing Ctrl+A to select an unfiltered large Tasks Table, then pressing it again, clears the initially loaded checkboxes but leaves offscreen rows selected. Scrolling reveals checked rows, while mouse clearing and a small filtered control clear correctly.
bugs.expected: Repeating the selection shortcut should consistently clear the selected result set rather than only its currently loaded rows.
bugs.actual: Pressing Ctrl+A to select an unfiltered large Tasks Table, then pressing it again, clears the initially loaded checkboxes but leaves offscreen rows selected. Scrolling reveals checked rows, while mouse clearing and a small filtered control clear correctly.
reproSteps: Open an unfiltered Tasks Table with enough records to require virtual scrolling.
Press Ctrl+A to select all, then repeat Ctrl+A to clear.
Compare clear initial rows with the remaining selected count, then scroll to reveal checked rows.
Compare a small filtered result and the ordinary mouse clear control.

bugs.name: Teammate view links silently fall back to another view
bugs.summary: Opening an owner’s saved unlisted filtered Company view URL as another workspace member retains that viewId in the URL but displays All Companies without its saved filter. A saved Workspace-visible view URL opens with the correct filter; People shows the same fallback variation.
bugs.expected: Under the documented teammate-link sharing promise, a direct saved-view link should restore that view’s configuration or clearly explain that it is unavailable.
bugs.actual: Opening an owner’s saved unlisted filtered Company view URL as another workspace member retains that viewId in the URL but displays All Companies without its saved filter. A saved Workspace-visible view URL opens with the correct filter; People shows the same fallback variation.
reproSteps: As an owner, save an unlisted Company view with a narrow Name filter and retain its direct URL.
Open that exact URL as another ordinary workspace member and inspect the view name, filter and results.
Compare a Workspace-visible saved view link and the owner opening the original link.

bugs.name: Select-all header becomes partial after a large scroll jump
bugs.summary: After selecting all Company rows, one large virtual-scroll jump changes the header checkbox to indeterminate while the selected total is unchanged and visible rows remain checked. Gradual settled scrolling keeps the header checked.
bugs.expected: The header checkbox should accurately represent the same complete selection across virtual scrolling.
bugs.actual: After selecting all Company rows, one large virtual-scroll jump changes the header checkbox to indeterminate while the selected total is unchanged and visible rows remain checked. Gradual settled scrolling keeps the header checked.
reproSteps: Open an ungrouped Company Table and select all rows.
Perform one large vertical scroll jump and inspect the header, visible row checks and selected total.
Reload and compare gradual settled scrolling to the same region.

bugs.name: Copied Calendar view resets its saved period to Month
bugs.summary: Creating a view from a saved Calendar configuration uses Month instead of the source Week or Day period. The copied period persists while the source configuration remains intact.
bugs.expected: Copying the current saved Calendar view should preserve its selected period along with the configuration being copied.
bugs.actual: Creating a view from a saved Calendar configuration uses Month instead of the source Week or Day period. The copied period persists while the source configuration remains intact.
reproSteps: Save a Calendar view in Week or Day and verify that selection.
Create a new view from the current view through the ordinary copy route.
Inspect the new Calendar period and reload; compare the retained source period.

bugs.name: Hide empty hides populated Opportunity columns after a drag
bugs.summary: With Hide empty enabled, dragging an Opportunity into an initially empty configured Stage can leave the now-populated destination hidden. The count remains populated; reload exposes the saved card. In the tested filtered view, moving all displayed cards can leave a blank board.
bugs.expected: Hide empty should hide empty columns and show a configured column after it receives a card.
bugs.actual: With Hide empty enabled, dragging an Opportunity into an initially empty configured Stage can leave the now-populated destination hidden. The count remains populated; reload exposes the saved card. In the tested filtered view, moving all displayed cards can leave a blank board.
reproSteps: Create a disposable Opportunities Kanban view with configured Stage groups and enable Hide empty.
Move a fresh card into an initially empty destination Stage.
Observe the missing populated destination despite the count; reload to reveal the saved card. Repeat with fresh data and compare the initial visible populated column.

bugs.name: Fresh mobile Date filter clips the calendar controls
bugs.summary: Opening a newly added Date filter at 390px clips the calendar’s Saturday column and next-month arrow. Desktop and reopening the same popup expose those controls; horizontal scrolling does not recover the clipped edge in the fresh popup.
bugs.expected: A visible Date filter calendar should expose its day columns and month navigation within the popup.
bugs.actual: Opening a newly added Date filter at 390px clips the calendar’s Saturday column and next-month arrow. Desktop and reopening the same popup expose those controls; horizontal scrolling does not recover the clipped edge in the fresh popup.
reproSteps: At 390px in a fresh Table view, add a Due Date Is filter and open its calendar.
Inspect the clipped rightmost day column and next-month control.
Compare desktop and reopening the same mobile popup, then select a previously clipped day.

bugs.name: Returning from a record resets Kanban scroll position
bugs.summary: Returning through a record breadcrumb remounts the Kanban board at the top-left, losing its previous browsing position.
bugs.expected: Returning from a Task record through its breadcrumb should restore the previous Kanban browsing position.
bugs.actual: Independent judges reproduced a vertical and horizontal reset while the By Status view remained selected. Side-panel closure preserves position, and the Table breadcrumb restores its opened row. The Kanban restoration implementation had been removed in a native-scrolling migration.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded Apple workspace and open Tasks > By Status.
Scroll down the Kanban board about 1,200 pixels and note a visible card. At a narrow viewport, also scroll horizontally to another column.
Open a task in its full record page, then return using the Tasks breadcrumb.
Observe that By Status remains selected but the board returns to the top-left.

bugs.name: Adding a Company Kanban group resets grouping to Stage and empties the board
bugs.summary: In Opportunities → By Stage, changing Group by to Company works until a company group is added. Selecting Google in New group resets the grouping field to Stage while retaining incompatible group configuration, leaving the board blank. Reproduced twice.
bugs.expected: Google should appear as a Company column containing its two opportunities, and Group should remain Company after adding the group and reloading.
bugs.actual: After selecting Google the entire board disappears. Options shows Group: Stage instead of Company. Reload retains the broken blank board (view count becomes 2). Selecting Group by Stage again restores stage columns.
reproSteps: Open the built-in Opportunities By Stage Kanban and change Group by to Company or Owner.
Allow the grouping update to complete, then add a matching relation group through New group.
Reopen Group settings and observe grouping has reverted to Stage while relation group values remain. Reload and inspect the saved board.
Compare a newly created custom board grouped by Company with an explicitly added Company group.

bugs.name: Changing a Kanban aggregate silently clears active filters
bugs.summary: On Tasks → By Status, changing the column aggregation discards an applied Title filter and expands the board from 150 matching tasks to all 1,800. Reproduced with Count all and Count empty → Title.
bugs.expected: Changing the aggregation preserves the active Title filter and the 150 matching records. Saving an unrelated view setting must not silently discard the current filter.
bugs.actual: The Title filter chip and Update view disappear, and the board expands to all 1,800 tasks. Count all shows 1,050 / 525 / 225 across columns instead of the filtered 150 / 0 / 0. Reapplying the filter and choosing Count empty → Title clears it again.
reproSteps: Open Tasks By Status and apply a Title Contains filter matching a subset of records. Leave the filter pending and confirm Update view appears.
Change a column calculation to Count all or Count empty for Title.
Observe the pending filter chip and Update view disappear and unfiltered Tasks return.
Save the filter before changing the calculation as a passing control.

bugs.name: Saved Opportunity Stage board reopens with no columns or cards
bugs.summary: The existing Opportunities → By Stage saved board shows a record count of 150 but renders an empty board after reload. Switching Group by from Stage to Owner and back to Stage restores populated columns only until the next reload. Reproduced after a fresh sign-in; a newly created board did not reproduce this failure.
bugs.expected: The saved Stage grouping should reopen with its five populated columns and allow browsing the 150 matching opportunities.
bugs.actual: The toolbar shows By Stage · 150, while the board is completely blank with no columns, cards, or empty-state explanation. Cycling Group by temporarily restores the board; reload loses it again. The same blank state remained after a fresh browser session and sign-in.
reproSteps: Open the populated built-in Opportunities By Stage board.
Change Group by to Owner or Company, then change it back to Stage. Observe the populated Stage columns return live.
Reload and wait for the record count to load. Observe no Stage columns/cards and no configured visible groups.
Compare the same round trip on a freshly created custom Stage board.

bugs.name: People 'Search any field' with several words returns records that match any word, not all words
bugs.summary: On the People list, a 'Search any field' filter with more than one word returns the union of matches for each word. Searching 'John Gonzalez' returns 50 people, including Debbie Johnson and John Cook, when only John Gonzalez matches the full term.
bugs.expected: A multi-token full-name search should require every entered name token to match a name component. This does not require literal phrase matching, token order, or distribution across unrelated fields.
bugs.actual: The view shows '· 50' records. That is exactly the 42 'john' matches plus the 9 'gonzalez' matches, minus the 1 overlap. Results include Debbie Johnson, John Guerrero, Theodore Gonzalez, John Cook, Nathaniel Johnson, etc. Likewise 'Red Hat' returns Meredith Gregory, who matches only the substring 'red'.
reproSteps: Open the People list and use Search any field.
Search a first-name token, then a last-name token, and note their separate matching sets.
Search both tokens together for a known full name. Observe first-name-only and last-name-only records remain.
Compare an ordinary multiword text-field match; this entry concerns full-name token matching rather than a literal phrase or arbitrary cross-field token distribution.

bugs.name: Calendar card selection never activates the selection toolbar
bugs.summary: Calendar cards expose working checkboxes but their selected state is not reflected in the list header, unlike Table and Kanban.
bugs.expected: Checked calendar records should activate the same selected-count and selection-action toolbar provided by Table and Kanban, or the calendar should not offer unsupported selection controls.
bugs.actual: Both People checkboxes have aria-checked=true, but the header remains People / New Person, with no '2 selected' indicator or Update/selection actions. Tasks likewise checks the selected record (including all four date appearances of that record) without any selected count or toolbar. Table and Kanban selections correctly activate the toolbar in independent tests.
reproSteps: Create or open a populated Month Calendar view for People or Tasks.
Hover a card and select its checkbox. Select a second card when available.
Observe the cards checked while the header still shows the ordinary New action without the selected count or selection actions.
Compare selecting records in a Table or Kanban view, where the selection actions activate.

bugs.name: Existing saved views lose their record area after layout or grouping changes
bugs.summary: Existing Tasks By Status and Opportunities By Stage views become blank after changing their layout/grouping. The views retain record counts and settings but lose all visible records and groups after reload. Newly created custom views render successfully.
bugs.expected: Changing layout or grouping should preserve a usable saved view. Calendar should render its grid; a Stage Kanban should regenerate and persist stage columns.
bugs.actual: Tasks By Status shows 1,800 records but a completely blank record area, including after reload. Opportunities By Stage shows 150 records but no columns/cards after the grouping round trip and reload; its Group settings show Stage but no visible groups. Newly created custom views can render these layouts. By Stage's saved groups are empty, as are the affected By Status groups. Screenshot of Tasks failure: tasks-calendar-blank.png.
reproSteps: Open the built-in Tasks By Status view and change Layout to Calendar.
Close Options, wait, reload, and choose a populated date field such as Due Date. Observe the record area lacks the Calendar grid.
Switch the affected view back to Kanban and reload; inspect the absent groups/cards.
Compare a newly created custom Calendar view and its reload.

bugs.name: Save as new view fails when changing a table to Kanban
bugs.summary: Saving a filtered Opportunities table as a new Kanban view fails with a missing main-group field error although Stage is shown as selected. Creating a Kanban through Add view works.
bugs.expected: A new Kanban saved view should be created with Stage grouping and the Amount filter retained.
bugs.actual: No view is created or opened. An error toast says 'Kanban view must have a main group by field', despite Stage being displayed in the form. Create becomes disabled and remains disabled even after reselecting Stage. Reproduced twice, including with a one-second pause after selecting Kanban. Screenshot: save-as-kanban-missing-group.png.
reproSteps: Open Opportunities All Opportunities in Table layout and apply a valid Amount filter.
Choose Save as new view, enter a name, and change View type to Kanban. Confirm Stage is displayed as selected.
Wait for the form to settle and click Create. Observe the missing-main-group-field error and no new view.
Reselect Stage and inspect the still-disabled Create control. Compare creating a Kanban through Add view.

bugs.name: Amount filter accepts comma-formatted numbers but returns incorrect records
bugs.summary: An Opportunities Amount threshold containing thousands separators is accepted and displayed but returns records below the threshold.
bugs.expected: Normalize comma-formatted numeric thresholds to their equivalent numeric value, or reject unsupported formatting with a clear validation error.
bugs.actual: Amount greater than or equal to 1000000 returns 33 matching records; entering 1,000,000 displays the threshold without an error but returns all 150 records, including amounts of 450k and 320k. Switching back restores the correct result; the comma failure was observed twice.
reproSteps: Open Opportunities and select All Opportunities.
Apply an Amount greater-than-or-equal filter with 1000000 and observe the matching records.
Edit the threshold to 1,000,000, press Enter and close the filter menu.
Observe records below the displayed threshold and an expanded result count without a validation error.
Restore 1000000 and compare the results, then repeat the comma-formatted input.
